You use before and after as conjunctions to join two clauses stating the order in which the actions happen.

You can use before and after between two events.

Use before when you want to say that an action is a requirement for another action to happen, or that an action will happen first and then a second action will take place.

Example:
We need to have an object before using prototype based programming.

In this example, it is necessary to have an object to be able to program using prototype based programming.

Use after to talk about an action that happens later in time in relation to another action.

Example:
Clone an object after you see that you can copy its behavior to another object.

Be careful when using a verb next to before, because you need to make sure it ends in –ing form.

Professor: Hi, guys! Before starting, I want you to have clear some major concepts related to the programming activities we have to develop in class.
Richard: Cool! I need to know some features to differentiate those programming activities after the explanation, is that okay?
Professor: Sure! Let's start by reviewing prototype-based programming, okay?
Richard: Well, prototype-based is a style of OOP.
Professor: Now, can you tell me what a prototype is and what OOP means?
Richard: Well, OOP refers to a programming language model. Now, prototype-based programming is similar to OOP but in this model, you reuse those prototypical objects for creating a new group of information.
Professor: Right, so you copy specific, generic information for reusing it into huge, new, informational lists.

Richard: Now, after you explain that, it is necessary to know the first prototype programming language.
Professor: Sure! Let's talk about Self.
Richard: Self is the first prototype-oriented programming language which looks for usual, researchable topics in object-oriented designs.
Professor: Exactly! Of course, after its creation, people wanted to develop more programming languages that supported the dynamic dispatching of their delegation.

Richard: Cool! Delegation is the correct and most effective method to find a match according to the prototypes of the different, big, round groups of objects. Delegation features allow us to find the right piece of simple data before finding a common prototype in different groups. That's why prototype-based language refers to slots.
Professor: Well Richard, I think you are ready to present the test.
Richard: I need to study the information we reviewed before taking the test, but I will hope for the best.
